Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 95bc5c225513fc3c4ce169563fb5e3929fbb938b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "matteo.cotifava" <cotifavamatteo@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 22:54:12 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] ASoC: soc-core: flush delayed work before removing DAIs and
 widgets

When a sound card is unbound while a PCM stream is open, a
use-after-free can occur in snd_soc_dapm_stream_event(), called from
the close_delayed_work workqueue handler.

During unbind, snd_soc_unbind_card() flushes delayed work and then
calls soc_cleanup_card_resources(). Inside cleanup,
snd_card_disconnect_sync() releases all PCM file descriptors, and
the resulting PCM close path can call snd_soc_dapm_stream_stop()
which schedules new delayed work with a pmdown_time timer delay.
Since this happens after the flush in snd_soc_unbind_card(), the
new work is not caught. soc_remove_link_components() then frees
DAPM widgets before this work fires, leading to the use-after-free.

The existing flush in soc_free_pcm_runtime() also cannot help as it
runs after soc_remove_link_components() has already freed the widgets.

Add a flush in soc_cleanup_card_resources() after
snd_card_disconnect_sync() (after which no new PCM closes can
schedule further delayed work) and before soc_remove_link_dais()
and soc_remove_link_components() (which tear down the structures the
delayed work accesses).

Fixes: e894efef9ac7 ("ASoC: core: add support to card rebind")
Signed-off-by: Matteo Cotifava <cotifavamatteo@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260309215412.545628-3-cotifavamatteo@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

diff --git a/sound/soc/soc-core.c b/sound/soc/soc-core.c
index e5ac8ae1665d..cf826c2a8b59 100644
--- a/sound/soc/soc-core.c
+++ b/sound/soc/soc-core.c
@@ -2121,6 +2121,9 @@ static void soc_cleanup_card_resources(struct snd_soc_card *card)
 	for_each_card_rtds(card, rtd)
 		if (rtd->initialized)
 			snd_soc_link_exit(rtd);
+	/* flush delayed work before removing DAIs and DAPM widgets */
+	snd_soc_flush_all_delayed_work(card);
+
 	/* remove and free each DAI */
 	soc_remove_link_dais(card);
 	soc_remove_link_components(card);
-- 
2.34.1

In this patch, the fix is applied to a single file: `sound/soc/soc-core.c`.

### Modifications in the file:
- A call to `snd_soc_flush_all_delayed_work(card)` is inserted inside `soc_cleanup_card_resources()`, after the loop that initializes and exits each runtime (via `snd_soc_link_exit`) and just before the removal of DAIs (`soc_remove_link_dais`) and components (`soc_remove_link_components`).

### Relationship of modifications:
The bug occurred because during card unbind, `snd_card_disconnect_sync()` releases PCM file descriptors, and the resulting close path can schedule new delayed work (with a `pmdown_time` delay). This scheduled work was not flushed before tearing down DAPM widgets and DAIs, leading to a use-after-free when the delayed work later accessed freed structures.

The added `flush` call ensures that any delayed work (which may access DAPM widgets or DAIs) is completed **after** all new work from PCM close has been scheduled (i.e., after `snd_card_disconnect_sync`) and **before** the structures are removed. This prevents the race condition. The existing flush in `snd_soc_unbind_card()` came too early, and the flush in `soc_free_pcm_runtime()` came too late. The new placement closes the gap.

Root cause:
During card unbind, `snd_card_disconnect_sync()` triggers PCM close calls that can schedule delayed work (`close_delayed_work`) with a `pmdown_time` timer delay. This work is scheduled after the initial flush in `snd_soc_unbind_card()`, so it is not caught. Subsequently, `soc_remove_link_components()` frees DAPM widgets before the delayed work executes, causing a use-after-free in `snd_soc_dapm_stream_event()`. The fix adds a proper flush in `soc_cleanup_card_resources()` after all possible new work is scheduled and before the structures are torn down.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
snd_card_disconnect_sync(card->snd_card);
soc_remove_link_components(card);
Reason:
During card unbind, `snd_card_disconnect_sync()` triggers PCM close calls that can schedule delayed work (`close_delayed_work`) via `snd_soc_dapm_stream_stop()`. This work is scheduled after the earlier flush in `snd_soc_unbind_card()` and before the teardown of DAPM widgets. Subsequently, `soc_remove_link_components()` frees the DAPM widgets that the delayed work accesses, leading to a use-after-free when the work eventually executes.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
snd_soc_flush_all_delayed_work(card);
Reason:
This flush is added after `snd_card_disconnect_sync()` (after which no new PCM closes can schedule further delayed work) and before `soc_remove_link_dais()` and `soc_remove_link_components()` (which tear down the structures the delayed work accesses). It ensures that any delayed work scheduled during the PCM close path is completed before the relevant DAPM widgets and DAIs are removed, thus preventing the use-after-free.
